narrative:
The model estimates a 94% chance that you will leave your current job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability reflects patterns the system sees in your overall profile compared to others who tend to stay.

The three factors that most strongly shaped this outlook, in order of importance, were your total years of professional experience, the time you have spent in your current role, and whether you have received other job offers while working here. 

Your 6–10 years of overall experience is less common among people the model expects to stay; most who remain have either very short or much longer careers. Similarly, having spent only 1–5 years in this organization places you in the group more likely to move on. Finally, the fact that you have received external job opportunities further tilts the prediction toward leaving, as this is a known signal that someone may soon depart.

Taken together, these elements created a clear picture for the model that you are at high risk of exiting. The organization should discuss your career goals with you openly and explore whether better support, recognition, or growth opportunities could change your outlook. You may also want to reflect on what would make staying feel more worthwhile before making any decisions. (218 words)
